This looks like a corrugated plate for a heat exchanger (TES15 is probably a plate for a thermal energy system or an exchanger). However, the description only says it is an alloy steel sheet that has been corrugated, and does not state a specific use.

Heat exchanger plates would fall under 8419.90. Without a stated use, the classification would be by material, as a steel article.

The description says "SI-Steel", which suggests silicon electrical steel. Grade 500B400 sounds like an electrical steel grade, such as M400-50A with a 0.5 mm thickness. Electrical steel laminations are typically 0.5 mm thick. Silicon electrical steel falls under 7225 or 7226 if it is alloy steel, and the grain-oriented/non-oriented split applies there. A corrugated shape would be further worked than rolled, so it may not stay in chapter 72. Chapter 72 covers flat-rolled products that are "corrugated" only if they are not further worked. The note on flat-rolled products includes products with patterns in relief derived directly from rolling, but a corrugation done after rolling would be further worked. That moves it to 7326 (other articles of iron or steel) or 7616 for aluminum. Forged or stamped articles fall under 7326.19 or 7326.90.

The 7326.90 subheading is the best fit for other articles of iron or steel. The statistical suffix 7326.90.8688 is the usual "other" line, so I'll use that.
